title: Implement deferred trace enrichment and token-cost triage
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Incident postmortems showed we were losing context for long-tail invocations and warmup-related token cost spikes because enrichment of traces (KV cache state, kernel selection, prefetch hints) was done synchronously or not at all. That produced noisy alerts and made root cause triage slow. This PR introduces a deferred trace enrichment pipeline plus a token-cost triage surface to make attribution and alerting actionable. Scope: 1) a compact enrichment proto and storage schema for attaching warmed-state and kernel metadata to sampled traces; 2) a background hydrator service (deferred-enricher) that consumes compact trace anchors and hydrates them asynchronously into trace objects; 3) a sampling/promotion policy that biases enrichment toward long-tail token spikes, coldstarts, and prefetch misses; 4) a set of dashboards and an alert decomposition rule that attribute token cost and latency to invocation phases (parse/encode/kv-cache/gen/kernel) and to kernel/backpressure labels; 5) e2e and unit tests plus docs. Operational properties: enrichment is opt-in via an org-level feature flag for Private/Dedicated customers; hydrator runs with rate-limited workers and backpressure; enriched data is TTL'd and stored in a compact bucket to limit storage cost. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout for 10% of traffic in staged environments, monitor false-positive suppression metrics and CI e2e, then increase to 50% then 100% if noise decreases. Related work: ties into ENG-4219 (token-triage roadmap) and ENG-5132 (kv-cache profiler).
commits: 3 commits: (1) core: add enrichment proto, store schema, and serialization helpers; (2) service: deferred-enricher implementation, worker pool, backpressure and instrumentation; (3) observability: dashboards token-cost-triage.json, alert rule token-decompose.yaml, e2e tests and docs update.

review_comments: Ben Clarke: Please ensure enrichment payloads cannot leak PII and that we apply redaction early in the hydrator. Response (Asha): Redaction is implemented at serialization boundary and enforced by schema; added unit tests demonstrating redaction for masked fields. Maya Gupta: The sampling bias looks reasonable but can we add a circuit breaker for when enrichment queue growth exceeds threshold? Response (Asha): Added queue-growth breaker and metrics (enricher.queue_length, enricher.rejects) and a config knob with safe defaults. Luca Romano: Two nit picks: prefer context-aware cancellation in worker.go and move magic constants to configs. Response (Asha): Addressed both, updated worker to respect context cancellation and extracted constants; ran lint and local stress tests. After changes reviewers approved and gave LGTM. CI noted a flaky e2e test on first run; rerun passed. Deploy/merge notes: merged via squash and merge after green CI and sign-off from reviewers.
ci_summary: CI pipeline: unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), integration (pass), e2e (flaky-first-run then pass on retry). Coverage delta: +0.6% in telemetry package.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in deferred trace enrichment service to attach KV/cache and kernel metadata to sampled traces, and a token-cost triage dashboard and alert decomposition rule. Feature is feature-flagged and rolled out gradually. Improves token-level attribution and reduces noisy warmup alerts.
notes_for_oncall: If enricher queue_length grows above 10k or enricher.rejects > 0.1% for 10m, scale hydrator workers or disable feature-flag. Enricher emits metrics enricher.queue_length, enricher.process_latency_ms, enricher.rejects and sample enrichment rates per model/model-variant.
upgrade_instructions: No schema-migration required for existing traces. To enable: set feature flag telemetry.deferred_enrichment.enabled=true and configure hydrator replicas and queue size. Consult docs/observability/deferred-enrichment.md for knob recommendations.
